svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: An interactive-style static botany lab. A labelled cross-section of an angiosperm with numbered slots, a word bank of ten draggable-style term tiles, an instruction panel, a pollination inset, and Hint / Check Answer / Reset pop-ups toggled with pure CSS.
svg.text: Interactive botany lab · label the parts of an angiosperm
Match each numbered slot to a flower part

g.text: Study the labelled flower and trace each leader line.
Pick a term from the Word Bank at the bottom.
Drop it on the dashed slot with the matching number.
Press Check Answer for the key — or tap Hint when stuck.

svg.text: Drag a label onto its matching numbered slot

g.text: Stamen = the male part — a slender filament
Pistil (carpel) = the female part. Pollen lands on
the sticky stigma, then grows down the style to the ovary.
Sepals are the small green flaps (calyx) that
protected the bud; petals are the showy coloured blades.
The receptacle is the thickened tip of the stalk
where every floral part is attached.
Each numbered slot matches one term:
Stamen = Anther + Filament · Pistil = Stigma + Style + Ovary
Sepals + Petals = the protective & attractive outer whorls.
All ten labels have been returned to the Word Bank and
Drag each term onto the slot its leader line points to,
then press Check Answer to see how you did.
(This is a fully static SVG demo — nothing is saved.)
